title: Sort Integers by Binary Reflection
summary: Given an integer array, sort it in ascending order based on the binary reflection of each element.
statement: Given an integer array, sort it in ascending order based on the binary reflection of each element. If two elements have the same binary reflection, maintain their original order by keeping the smaller number first.
constraints: Reflect a positive integer by reversing the digits of its binary representation, then interpreting that result as binary.
Sort values by increasing reflected value.
Break reflected-value ties by the smaller original integer.
hints: Convert each value to binary without its prefix.
Reverse those bits and parse them in base two.
Use reflected value as the primary sort key and original value as the secondary key.
Tuple sorting implements both ascending rules deterministically.
editorial: Tuple sorting implements both ascending rules deterministically.

tests.explanation: Four reflects to one while five reflects to five, so both fours precede five.
Their reflected keys are three, three, and five; the tie places three before six.
